heroImage.alt: Maya the quokka and Kenji the koala chatting over coffee (AI-generated scene)

maya: Everyone makes mistakes in English. We just make ours on camera!
kenji: Watch, play, then comment your own sentence. We read them!
quiz: I am agree with you.
I agree with you.
I am agreeing you.
I agreed with you am.
"Agree" is a verb, so we don't add "am".
She don't like coffee.
She doesn't like coffee.
She not like coffee.
She isn't like coffee.
With he, she or it, use "doesn't".
I have 25 years old.
I'm 25 years old.
I have 25 years.
I am having 25 years.
In English we say our age with "be": I'm 25.
Can you explain me the rules?
Can you explain the rules to me?
Can you explain me about the rules?
Can you explain to me the rules me?
We explain something to someone.
I'm living in Sydney since March.
I've been living in Sydney since March.
I live in Sydney since March.
I was living in Sydney since March.
With "since", use the present perfect: I've been living / I've lived.
Let's discuss about the course.
Let's discuss the course.
Let's discuss on the course.
Let's discussing the course.
"Discuss" needs no "about". You can say "talk about" instead.
I look forward to hear from you.
I look forward to hearing from you.
I look forward hear from you.
I look forward for hearing from you.
After "look forward to", use the -ing form.
How much hours do you work?
How many hours do you work?
How much hour do you work?
How many hour you work?
Hours can be counted, so we say "how many".
